bottleneck: Longevity-associated genes like Klotho extend healthspan in mice, but human evidence is correlational: no trial has shown a longevity gene therapy extends human health or lifespan. Dosing a pleiotropic hormone-like protein systemically risks off-target effects across kidney, brain, and vasculature, and the decades-long endpoints make trials nearly impossible to run — no company can fund a 30-year study, and no regulator has defined what an aging indication would require.
current_state: Klotho and similar longevity factors are in early preclinical and small clinical studies for specific diseases, not aging itself. Aging as a therapeutic indication has no regulatory pathway anywhere.

sources.title: Gene Therapy: A Breakthrough in Disease Treatment

title: Longevity gene therapies lack human evidence
why_it_blocks: Aging kills more than any disease, yet no longevity intervention can be tested on aging timescales within any feasible trial. The endpoint problem freezes the field in mouse data while the largest cause of death goes unaddressed.
